text:
Hi everyone, I like to discuss an API question with you, first topic and background:

We're working out segwit templates (P2WPKH and P2WSH) and segwit addresses for LibBitcoin, looking forward to contribute this code to LB.

elements.text: To do this well and systematically, we thought, how should this stuff be done from the perspective of the LibBitcoin C++ API user, and therefore we figured that we should write a C++ usecase-example program that illustrates what a user normally wants to use the LibBitcoin API for with respect to non-segwit templates and addresses (P2PKH and P2SH), and then design the segwit additions out of a motivation that they should mean gentle variations to the non-segwit usecase code, or at least be symmetric.

text: To do this well and systematically, we thought, how should this stuff be done from the perspective of the LibBitcoin C++ API user, and therefore we figured that we should write a C++ usecase-example program that illustrates what a user normally wants to use the LibBitcoin API for with respect to non-segwit templates and addresses (P2PKH and P2SH), and then design the segwit additions out of a motivation that they should mean gentle variations to the non-segwit usecase code, or at least be symmetric.

elements.text:
The usecases we figured are:
 * from a public key (and mainnet vs testnet choice), generate P2PKH address
 * parse P2PKH or P2SH address - confirm valid, confirm testnet vs mainnet, print binary dump of payload
 * generate a Bitcoin TX output payload from a P2PKH or P2SH address
 * generate a Bitcoin TX input payload according to P2PKH template, from a private key, a TXID and output index
 * generate an unsigned Bitcoin TX input payload according to P2SH template, from a script
 * generate a Bitcoin TX, with one signed input according to P2PKH template, from a private key,
   a TXID and output index, and an output to a P2PKH address
 * generate a Bitcoin TX, with one signed input according to P2SH template, from a script, pushdata constants, a TXID and output index,
   and an output to a P2SH address
 * check if an Bitcoin TX input or output payload matches the p2pkh or p2sh pattern
 * extract Bitcoin address (always zero or one in count isn't it??) from Bitcoin TX input or output payload
 * ??? WIF serialization ???
 * ??? HD wallet xprv serialization ???
 * get list of transactions from txindex for given p2pkh/p2sh address

elements.text:
Now one thing that sticks out here, that I like to start our discussion with is, where in LB to implement the segwit addresses (i.e. P2WPKH and P2WSH).

All layers of LibBitcoin (e.g. client/server API etc.) use payment_address for describing a Bitcoin address.

With segwit, Bitcoin address now doesn't only mean P2PKH and P2SH, but also native (as bech32) and P2SH-wrapped (as p2sh) P2WPKH and P2WSH address.

Expectably of course the bech32 P2WPKH and P2WSH will be the more common addresses.



Our first thought was, let's make a witness_address class to describe this stuff.

But, second thought is, isn't Bitcoin a segwit phenomenon altogether now so we can as well just extend payment_address with segwit functionality?

As all LibBitcoin tooling does, and most dependencies likely do, want segwit template and address support, then with its introduction there will be code updates spread over all LB and dependency codebases
anyhow

.

payment_address can become a hybrid structure for both non-segwit and segwit addresses.

What are your thoughts on this topic?

Is there a goal, or not, in having LibBitcoin compile-able without segwit support and a separate witness_address class being needed for some such reason?

elements.text:
After having gotten clarified how the segwit (P2WPKH and P2WSH in bech32 and p2sh-wrapped variants) should be represented by LibBitcoin, we look forward to going into figuring how to implement the transaction templates, both inputs and outputs.

The P2W* inputs will of course differ fundamentally from their non-segwit counterparts in that they have the witness structure too, so there will be some fundamental differences between how to do non-segwit and segwit stuff - here the transaction format is different right, and the ability to process non-segwit (witness-free) transactions will remain with LB, right.

I'm only pointing out that you've asked good questions and it's not clear to me at the moment either.
